entirely.definition: to a complete degree or to the full or entire extent (`whole' is often used informally for `wholly'); "he was wholly convinced"; "entirely satisfied with the meal"; "it was completely different from what we expected"; "was completely at fault"; "a totally new situation"; "the directions were all wrong"; "it was not altogether her fault"; "an altogether new approach"; "a whole new idea"; "she felt right at home"; "he fell right into the trap"

entreatingly.definition: in a beseeching manner; "`You must help me,' she said imploringly"

enviably.definition: in an enviable manner; "she was enviably fluent in French"

enviously.definition: with jealousy; in an envious manner; "he looked at his friend's new car jealously"

environmentally.definition: for the environment; "the new recycling policy is environmentally safe"

equably.definition: in an equable manner; "he is an equably cheerful fellow"

equally.definition: to the same degree (often followed by `as'); "they were equally beautiful"; "birds were singing and the child sang as sweetly"; "sang as sweetly as a nightingale"; "he is every bit as mean as she is"

equitably.definition: in an equitable manner; "the inheritance was equitably divided among the sisters"

equivocally.definition: in an ambiguous manner; "this letter is worded ambiguously"

erectly.definition: in a straight-backed manner; "the old man still walks erectly"

ergo.definition: (used as a sentence connector) therefore or consequently

erratically.definition: in an erratic unpredictable manner; "economic changes are proceeding erratically"

erroneously.definition: in a mistaken or erroneous manner; "he mistakenly believed it"

erst.definition: at a previous time; "at one time he loved her"; "her erstwhile writing"; "she was a dancer once"

eruditely.definition: with erudition; in an erudite manner; "he talked eruditely about Indian mythology"

eschatologically.definition: in relation to eschatology; "even atheists can be eschatologically minded"

especially.definition: to a distinctly greater extent or degree than is common; "he was particularly fussy about spelling"; "a particularly gruesome attack"; "under peculiarly tragic circumstances"; "an especially (or specially) cautious approach to the danger"

essentially.definition: in essence; at bottom or by one's (or its) very nature; "He is basically dishonest"; "the argument was essentially a technical one"; "for all his bluster he is in essence a shy person"

esthetically.definition: in a tasteful way; "this building is aesthetically very pleasing"

eternally.definition: for a limitless time; "no one can live forever"; "brightly beams our Father's mercy from his lighthouse evermore"- P.P.Bliss

ethically.definition: in an ethical manner; from an ethical point of view; according to ethics; "he behaved ethically"; "this is ethically unacceptable"

ethnically.definition: with respect to ethnicity; "the neighborhood is ethnically diverse"

euphemistically.definition: in a euphemistic manner; "his violent death was euphemistically referred to as a passing away"

evasively.definition: with evasion; in an evasive manner; "her husband seemed to know many of the people who were named, but he replied evasively when asked who they were"

evenhandedly.definition: without favoring one party, in a fair evenhanded manner; "deal fairly with one another"

evenly.definition: in equal amounts or shares; in a balanced or impartial way; "a class evenly divided between girls and boys"; "they split their winnings equally"; "deal equally with rich and poor"

eventually.definition: after an unspecified period of time or an especially long delay

ever.definition: at any time; "did you ever smoke?"; "the best con man of all time"

everlastingly.definition: for a limitless time; "no one can live forever"; "brightly beams our Father's mercy from his lighthouse evermore"- P.P.Bliss

evermore.definition: at any future time; in the future; "lead a blameless life evermore"

everyplace.definition: to or in any or all places; "You find fast food stores everywhere"; "people everywhere are becoming aware of the problem"; "he carried a gun everywhere he went"; "looked all over for a suitable gift"; (`everyplace' is used informally for `everywhere')

everywhere.definition: to or in any or all places; "You find fast food stores everywhere"; "people everywhere are becoming aware of the problem"; "he carried a gun everywhere he went"; "looked all over for a suitable gift"; (`everyplace' is used informally for `everywhere')

evidently.definition: unmistakably (`plain' is often used informally for `plainly'); "the answer is obviously wrong"; "she was in bed and evidently in great pain"; "he was manifestly too important to leave off the guest list"; "it is all patently nonsense"; "she has apparently been living here for some time"; "I thought he owned the property, but apparently not"; "You are plainly wrong"; "he is plain stubborn"

evilly.definition: in a wicked evil manner; "act wickedly"; "grin evilly"

evolutionarily.definition: in an evolutionary way; from an evolutionary point of view; "the mutation has been evolutionarily successful"

exactly.definition: indicating exactness or preciseness; "he was doing precisely (or exactly) what she had told him to do"; "it was just as he said--the jewel was gone"; "it has just enough salt"; "Properly speaking, all true work is religion."--Thomas Carlyle

exceedingly.definition: to an extreme degree; "extremely cold"; "extremely unpleasant"; "she is super smart"; "the night was deathly cold"; "as a child, I was deathly afraid of snakes"

excellently.definition: extremely well; "he did splendidly in the exam"; "we got along famously"

exceptionally.definition: to an exceptional degree; "it worked exceptionally well"

excessively.definition: to a degree exceeding normal or proper limits; "too big"

excitedly.definition: with excitement; in an excited manner; "she shook his hand excitedly"

excitingly.definition: in an exciting manner; "at the time of its appearance, the movie must have seemed excitingly new, even revolutionary"

exclusively.definition: without any others being included or involved; "was entirely to blame"; "a school devoted entirely to the needs of problem children"; "he works for Mr. Smith exclusively"; "did it solely for money"; "the burden of proof rests on the prosecution alone"; "a privilege granted only to him"

excruciatingly.definition: in a very painful manner; "the progress was agonizingly slow"

excusably.definition: in an excusable manner or to an excusable degree; "he was excusably late"

exhaustively.definition: in an exhaustive manner; "we searched the files thoroughly"

exorbitantly.definition: to an exorbitant degree; "prices are exorbitantly high in the capital"

expansively.definition: in an impressively expansive manner; "she managed to live rather expansively on her modest income"

expectantly.definition: in an expectant manner; "she looked at him expectantly"

expeditiously.definition: with efficiency; in an efficient manner; "he functions efficiently"

expensively.definition: in an expensive manner; "an expensively dressed little man turned a corner and approached her"

experimentally.definition: in an experimental fashion; "this can be experimentally determined"

expertly.definition: in an expert manner; "he repaired the TV set expertly"

explicitly.definition: in an explicit manner; "in his foreword Professor Clark puts it explicitly"

explosively.definition: suddenly and rapidly; "the population in Central America is growing explosively"

exponentially.definition: in an exponential manner; "inflation is growing exponentially"

expressively.definition: with expression; in an expressive manner; "she gave the order to the waiter, using her hands very expressively"

expressly.definition: with specific intentions; for the express purpose; "she needs the money expressly for her patients"

exquisitely.definition: in a delicate manner; "finely shaped features"; "her fine drawn body"

extensively.definition: in a widespread way; "oxidation ponds are extensively used for sewage treatment in the Midwest"

externally.definition: on or from the outside; "the candidate needs to be externally evaluated"

extortionately.definition: to an exorbitant degree; "prices are exorbitantly high in the capital"

extraordinarily.definition: extremely; "she was inordinately smart"; "it will be an extraordinarily painful step to negotiate"

extravagantly.definition: in an abundant manner; "they were abundantly supplied with food"; "he thanked her profusely"

extremely.definition: to a high degree or extent; favorably or with much respect; "highly successful"; "He spoke highly of her"; "does not think highly of his writing"; "extremely interesting"

exuberantly.definition: in an exuberant manner; "the exuberantly baroque decoration of the church"

exultantly.definition: in an exultant manner; "it was exultingly easy"

exultingly.definition: in an exultant manner; "it was exultingly easy"
